result.summary: Read docs/agents/design/REQ-021.md in full and apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts's new getWaitlistPosition function line by line against it (lines 219-272). Confirmed it uses only plain Drizzle eq/lt/and/or filters (imported at line 2: `import { and, eq, lt, or } from "drizzle-orm"`) -- no raw SQL string, no .execute()/sql`` escape hatch, no window function anywhere in the diff. The two-query shape matches §2.2 exactly: query 1 (lines 234-241) reads the target row's own created_at/admission by id, LIMIT 1; defensive null returns for not-found (line 245-247) and non-waitlisted (line 249-251) match §2.2 steps 1-2 exactly. Query 2 (lines 256-268) counts rows matching event_id + admission='waitlisted' + the ahead condition, and the ahead condition's OR/AND nesting (`lt(createdAt, target) OR (eq(createdAt,target) AND lt(id, target.id))`) is byte-for-byte the tie-break §2.3 specifies (created_at asc, id asc). Result is aheadRows.length + 1, matching §2.2 step 4's 1-based position. No interface anywhere in this diff (RegistrationOutcome, RegisterForEventResult) gained a position/rank field, matching §2.4's computed-never-stored design. I did NOT trust BACKEND-DEV's report and independently re-verified AC2 myself with my own fixture rather than re-running the committed test. Wrote a throwaway script (apps/bot/src/domain/__verify_ac2_scratch.ts, run via `npx tsx`, deleted immediately after use -- git status --porcelain confirmed clean before continuing) against the already-running scratch Postgres (bot-postgres-1, port 55432): seeded my own chapter/venue/event(capacity=0)/3 users, inserted 3 waitlisted registrations directly with strictly increasing created_at (not through registerForEvent), read the second row's position via getWaitlistPosition -> 2, captured its updated_at (2026-09-07T05:39:07.658Z), ran a raw `pool.query("UPDATE registrations SET admission = 'withdrawn' WHERE id = $1", [firstRowId])` touching only the first row, re-read the second row's updated_at -> byte-identical (2026-09-07T05:39:07.658Z, exact same value, not just close), re-read its position via getWaitlistPosition -> 1. Also independently exercised both defensive cases in the same script: an unknown registrationId returns null, and an 'admitted' (non-waitlisted) row's id returns null. All confirmed independently, not copied from BACKEND-DEV's report -- my own AC2 result: PASS. AC1 independently verified by reading apps/bot/src/handlers/registration.ts's wiring (lines 98-106): the one new call to getWaitlistPosition is gated on `outcome.kind === "waitlisted" && outcome.registrationId !== undefined`, inside the same pre-existing display-data conditional REQ-020 already ran -- no second lookup pass, matching design §3.1. composeRegistrationReply's waitlisted case (lines 123-133) builds the line list exactly per §3.2: prefix/title/dateTime, then the position line only when waitlistPosition !== null, then waitlistedWhatNext unconditionally; null triggers silent omission (§3.1/§6 open question 3), no placeholder/error text -- confirmed by reading, not assumed. apps/bot/src/handlers/registration.test.ts's two AC1 cases exercise this through a real bot.handleUpdate() dispatch (not a mock of the handler), confirming reply text contains 'waitlistedPositionPrefix 1' then 'waitlistedPositionPrefix 2' for consecutive waitlisted registrants against a fully-booked event -- read and consider this adequate independent coverage of AC1's live-dispatch path. AC3 independently re-run myself (not copied): `git grep -niE "waitlist.?(position|rank)" -- apps/bot/src` finds only getWaitlistPosition's own definition, its call sites, and its tests -- no column, cache, or persisted field. Separately grepped apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts for position/rank: only two documentation comments (schema.ts:158, :273, :288 -- these predate this diff, part of REQ-011's original schema annotation anticipating this exact requirement) and the unrelated pre-existing profiles.position (job title) column. No schema change in this diff at all (confirmed via `git diff master...HEAD -- apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts` -- empty), matching REQ-021.md §7's explicit no-new-schema statement. AC4: read registration.db.test.ts's new AC4 describe (lines 508-530) -- 1 admitted + 6 waitlisted against a capacity=1 event, all six return kind='waitlisted', zero refusal, and the last-inserted row's own computed position equals the full count (6), confirming the ranking still holds at this size. decideRegistrationOutcome (registration.ts:48-74, byte-identical to REQ-020, confirmed unchanged by diff) has no ceiling anywhere in its unconditional waitlisted fallback (row 8) -- read and agree this is a genuine proof-of-absence per design §5, not something that needed a new design element. Null-for-not-found/non-waitlisted (defensive case): confirmed tested twice over -- BACKEND-DEV's own two dedicated test cases in registration.db.test.ts (lines 470-497: 'returns null for a row that is not (or no longer) waitlisted' and 'returns null for an unknown registrationId') plus my own independent script reproduction above. Both code paths (§2.2 steps 1 and 2) are exercised, not just one. i18n wording check (waitlistedWhatNext): en.ts says "What happens next: you'll move up automatically as seats open." / ru.ts's equivalent. This states only that promotion happens automatically as seats open -- no timing bound ("within X minutes"), no mechanism claim (no mention of REQ-023's not-yet-built auto-promotion trigger internals). This is exactly the safer wording the design's own §6 open question 2 named as the recommended alternative ("you'll move up automatically as seats open" is safer than "we'll notify you within X minutes"). CONTENT-BA's placeholder-copy discipline (decisions/0002) is otherwise unaffected -- these are placeholder strings, final wording still CONTENT-BA's call, but the placeholder itself does not overpromise. PASS on this check. Domain logic outside handlers (decisions/0004): handlers/registration.ts's new code is exactly one function call (getWaitlistPosition) plus threading its return value into a presentation function (composeRegistrationReply, a plain switch building strings) -- no admission-state, capacity, ranking, or tie-break logic appears in the handler body. All ranking/tie-break logic lives in domain/registration.ts, framework-free (no grammY import in that file, confirmed by reading its full import list). Compliant. now()/current_timestamp check (decisions/0006): grepped registration.ts case-insensitively for now\(\)|current_timestamp -- the only match is the file's own header comment stating the negative constraint (line 12), no actual SQL now()/current_timestamp call anywhere in the diff. getWaitlistPosition takes no evaluation-time parameter at all because it has no time-dependent predicate -- its filters are event_id/admission/created_at-comparison-to-a-stored-value, not comparisons against the current clock. Compliant, and correctly so -- this function was never a candidate for that rule's violation in the first place, but I checked anyway rather than assuming. Schema/migration review (decisions/0005, S13): no migration in this diff at all -- confirmed by `git diff master...HEAD --stat` showing no apps/bot/src/db/migrations/* file and REQ-021.md §7's explicit no-schema-change statement, itself independently confirmed against the current apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts (registrations_waitlist_order_idx and all four columns this design reads already existed, unchanged). Not applicable this run. Workspace/build-output check: this diff adds no new npm workspace, does not rename apps/bot or apps/web, and does not move any build-output directory -- confirmed via `git diff master...HEAD --stat` (only existing files under apps/bot/src, i18n, docs, handoffs changed; no package.json touched). No scratch `docker build` required per my role file's trigger condition. COMMANDS RE-RUN MYSELF, REAL OUTPUT (all from repo root): `npm run lint` -> exit 0, 0 errors (2 pre-existing unrelated apps/web LCP warnings only, same as BACKEND-DEV's report and REQ-020's baseline). `npm run build` -> exit 0, both workspaces clean (apps/web Next.js build succeeded, apps/bot tsc -p tsconfig.json clean). `TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://bot:bot@localhost:55432/bot npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism` -> 16 files / 178 tests passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped -- matches BACKEND-DEV's reported count exactly, independently re-run by me against the same already-running scratch Postgres, not copied. Scope check: the diff touches exactly the files REQ-021.md §7 named as expected (domain/registration.ts, handlers/registration.ts, i18n/{types,ru,en}.ts, plus the two test files) and nothing else. No scope creep found.

LIMIT 1 + one SELECT count-shaped query) against a table/columns that already existed before this requirement, introduces no new PII field, no new auth/authorization surface, no new write path, and no new audit-log action.
